title: Foundations: Sweetheart Songs - The Complete Guide
summary: What Sweetheart Songs is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Sweetheart Songs songs: Love ballads are the slow dance of popular music: direct lyrics, swelling choruses, and melodies built for dedications. From doo-wop to power ballads to wedding first dances, the formula is devotion plus dynamics.

History: The 1950s doo-wop ballads, 1970s soft rock, 1980s power ballads, and 1990s R&B (Whitney Houston's I Will Always Love You, 1992 — the best-selling single by a woman) each owned the form.

How the songs work: Sweetheart Songs favors the keys of C, G, D, F, Bb. Common forms include Verse–chorus with a key-changing final chorus; The big bridge before the last chorus. Players should master the key change: up a half or whole step for the finale first, then strings swelling under the chorus. Capo 2 for sweet acoustic ballads.

title: Auld Lang Syne - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Auld Lang Syne, a public-domain Sweetheart Songs standard.
body:
Auld Lang Syne (Robert Burns, 1788. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Should auld acquaintance be forgot,
And never brought to mind?
Should auld acquaintance be forgot,
And auld lang syne?

Chorus:
For auld lang syne, my dear,
For auld lang syne,
We'll take a cup o' kindness yet,
For auld lang syne.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Sweetheart Songs accompaniment in C using the 'Ballad I–V–vi–IV' pattern:
C | G | Am | F

Technique: the key change: up a half or whole step for the finale. Capo 2 for sweet acoustic ballads.
facts: Form: Verse–chorus with a key-changing final chorus

title: I Will Always Love You - Sweetheart Songs Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for I Will Always Love You by Whitney Houston (Dolly Parton) (1992).
body:
I Will Always Love You — Whitney Houston (Dolly Parton), 1992. The best-selling single by a female artist ever.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of D):
D | G | Bm | A
